- MRCP findings — essential to confirm presence of multifocal strictures, beading, or dominant stricture; absence would weaken PSC diagnosis  
- Serum IgG4 level — critical to rule out IgG4-related cholangitis  
- CA 19-9 — needed to assess for cholangiocarcinoma, especially with focal duct dilatation  
- Hepatitis serologies — required to exclude chronic viral hepatitis as a cause of cholestasis and ductal changes  
- GGT — would reinforce cholestatic pattern and help distinguish hepatic vs. bone origin of ALP elevation  
- Liver biopsy — not yet performed; could show periductal fibrosis (“onion-skinning”) supportive of PSC if imaging is equivocal  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC)
